title: What were the main findings of WHO's World Malaria Report 2024?

sources.snippet: According to WHO's latest World malaria report, there were an estimated 263 million cases and 597 000 malaria deaths worldwide in 2023. This represents about 11 million more cases in 2023 compared to 2022, and nearly the same number of deaths.

answer:
The WHO World Malaria Report 2024 found that since 2000, an estimated 2.2 billion malaria cases and 12.7 million deaths have been averted [1]. However, malaria remains a serious global health threat: in 2023 there were an estimated 263 million cases and 597,000 deaths worldwide [1]. This was about 11 million more cases than in 2022, while the number of deaths was nearly the same [1][3][5]. Approximately 95% of the deaths occurred in the WHO African Region, where many at risk still lack access to prevention, detection, and treatment services [1].

The report highlighted positive trends in scaling up effective tools, including new-generation nets, malaria vaccines, and seasonal malaria chemoprevention [4]. It also introduced a first dedicated chapter on addressing inequity, emphasizing the need to reach vulnerable groups such as children under 5, women and girls, Indigenous Peoples, migrants, people with disabilities, and people in remote areas with limited healthcare access [1][6].
